newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish trader BEST sets IPO price at 58 zlotys.
newsitem.headline: Polish trader BEST sets IPO price at 58 zlotys.

text.p: Polish trading and financial operations firm BEST PH SA has set the issue price of its 1.5-million-share initial public offering at 58 zlotys each, the company's deputy president Janusz Krainski said on Monday.
Krainski said Wood and Company had undewritten two thirds of the issue and Polish Development Bank (PBR) one third. Their fee is 19.22 percent of the issue's value.
"Last Friday management set the issue price at the level of 58 zlotys," Krainski told a news conference.

BEST is offering 500,000 existing shares and one million new shares, with up to 400,000 existing shares and up to 800,000 new shares offered in a large-investor subscription from February 12 to February 21.
From February 17 to February 28 small investors will be offered 200,000 new shares and 100,000 existing shares.
The company, based in the northern city of Sopot and employing 311 people, seeks a listing on the bourse's main market.
BEST made a net profit of 3.1 million zlotys last year on sales of 34.3 million zlotys.
It expects to net 13.4 million zlotys, 23.3 million zlotys and 35.6 million zlotys in 1997, 1998 and 1999 respectively.
It said sales would rise to 48 million zlotys, 66.5 million zlotys and 90 million zlotys in those three years.
